channel.title: Apex Frames Blog
channel.description: Practical articles on choosing and installing windows and doors: uPVC vs aluminium, glazing, condensation, DoP and CE, what affects price.

item.title: uPVC or Aluminium Windows? How to Choose the Right One
item.description: Choose uPVC when you want good insulation at a lower cost for homes. Choose thermally broken aluminium when you need large openings, slim profiles or a commercial building. Both are long-lasting when certified and properly installed.

item.title: What Affects the Price of Windows and Doors?
item.description: Price depends on the profile system, size, glazing, opening type, colour, hardware and installation. Two quotes compare fairly only when they specify the same elements. Apex Frames gives no verbal prices: the price is written only in the detailed quote, after measurement.

item.title: Double or Triple Glazing? Argon, Low-E and How to Choose
item.description: Double glazing with argon gas and a Low-E coating is often enough for homes. Triple glazing insulates better but is heavier and costs more, so it makes sense for very cold rooms or when maximum insulation is required. The exact value always comes from the Declaration of Performance.

item.title: Why Do Windows Sweat? Condensation and How to Fix It
item.description: Condensation forms when warm, humid air meets a cold surface. It is usually not a defect but a sign of high humidity or insufficient ventilation. A better window lowers the risk, but ventilation remains essential.

item.title: Declaration of Performance (DoP) and CE Marking: How to Read Them
item.description: The Declaration of Performance (DoP) is the manufacturer’s document stating a window’s or door’s certified values, under EN 14351-1 and Regulation (EU) 305/2011. The CE marking shows the manufacturer takes responsibility for those values. Ask for both before ordering.

item.title: Strap or Motorised Shutters? Outside or Inside Box
item.description: Strap-operated shutters are the simple, economical choice; motorised shutters with remote control are more comfortable, especially for large openings. An outside box allows quick installation and easy access, while an inside box gives a cleaner look and better integration into the facade.

item.title: Window Installation in 8 Steps: What to Ask Your Installer
item.description: A good installation follows 8 steps: preliminary inspection, removal, frame fixing, PU perimeter insulation, airtight sealing, mechanical adjustment, final inspection and clean-up. Even the best window performs poorly if badly installed.

item.title: Sliding Doors: Lift & Slide, PSK or Standard?
item.description: Lift & slide doors suit large openings and comfortable daily use; standard sliding doors are the simplest solution; PSK combines tilt ventilation with parallel sliding; folding (bi-fold) doors open almost the full width. The choice depends on size, space at the side and budget.

item.title: How to Choose an Entrance Door: uPVC, Aluminium, Panel or Automatic
item.description: Choose an entrance door by use: uPVC or aluminium for homes and businesses, a solid panel for privacy and safety glass for light. For busy business entrances, an automatic sensor door is more practical. Define left or right opening from the outside before ordering.

item.title: What Is a Thermal Break in Aluminium Profiles?
item.description: A thermal break is an insulating separator inside the aluminium profile that interrupts heat flow from inside to outside and vice versa. Aluminium conducts heat well, so profiles without this separator lose energy quickly. The exact insulation value always comes from Uw in the Declaration of Performance.

item.title: Laminated or Tempered Glass? Which Is Safer
item.description: Laminated (triplex) glass has an interlayer between panes and holds fragments together if broken. Tempered glass is more impact-resistant and, when it breaks, turns into small pieces. For doors and balustrades one is chosen according to risk, and often both are combined when extra safety is required.

item.title: Cassette or Classic Awning? How to Choose for Your Terrace
item.description: A cassette awning protects the fabric when retracted and looks cleaner; classic models are simpler. A motor adds comfort, while a manual mechanism is more economical. For larger spaces, an aluminium pergola with or without a canopy is the alternative.

item.title: Which Colour for Your Windows: White, Anthracite or Woodgrain?
item.description: uPVC comes in white, woodgrain, black (Jet Black) and anthracite, even with a different colour inside and outside. Aluminium offers a wide RAL range and wood finishes. Choose by facade, shutters and interior look, and ask for samples before ordering.

item.title: Glass Curtain Wall Facades: What to Know Before the Project
item.description: A curtain wall facade is an insulated aluminium structure with glazing that clads the building facade and does not carry its weight. It is built to the architect’s design, with custom dimensions, divisions and RAL colours and with thermal, solar-control or laminated glass.

item.title: How to Reduce Street Noise with New Windows
item.description: Noise insulation depends on four things: the glass (acoustic or laminated), the seals and profile, airtight installation and ventilation. The Rw value in the Declaration of Performance shows the insulation: the higher, the less noise gets through. An open or leaky window cancels the effect.

item.title: Insect Screens: Which Type to Choose for a Door or Window
item.description: For balcony doors, plissé (pleated) or sliding screens are usually chosen; for windows, vertical roll-up or fixed-frame screens. The mesh is fibreglass or polyester with UV protection, and the modular plissé system has from 1 to 4 leaves.

item.title: Glass, Stainless and Aluminium Railings: What to Know Before Ordering
item.description: Glass railings protect a balcony, terrace or staircase without cutting the view. The structure is stainless steel or aluminium and the glass is safety glass, laminated or tempered. They are made to on-site measurements; height and safety requirements are set by the project and building rules.
